definition_zh: 斑马；斑马条纹；斑马线；黑白相间的
definition_en: an African wild horse with black and white stripes all over its body
core_image: 草原上一匹满身黑白条纹的马，正在低头吃草
scene: 非洲草原上，一小群斑马穿过金黄的草丛，黑白条纹在阳光里格外醒目。At dawn, a small herd of zebra crossed the grassland in bright light.
sceneCN: 这里 zebra 是「斑马」的意思（第 1 个义项：身上有黑白条纹的非洲野马）；句意：黎明时分，一小群斑马在明亮的光线中穿过草原。

pos.zh: 斑马条纹；黑白条纹图案
黑白相间的；斑马条纹的

collocations.zh: 细纹斑马（一种受保护的斑马）

derivatives.zh: 由 zebra 加类后缀 -oid 构成，义为「斑马与马或驴杂交的后代」
由 zebra 加 -ina 构成的植物或动物名，如吊竹梅一类
由 zebra 与 fish 复合而成，义为「斑马鱼」，是常用实验动物

senses.title: The striped African horse
senses.definition: a wild horse of African grasslands, with black and white stripes all over its body
senses.definitionCN: 生活在非洲草原上、全身有黑白条纹的野马
senses.example: A zebra can run very fast when a lion appears.
senses.exampleCN: 狮子出现时，斑马能跑得非常快。
senses.why: The name enters English through Portuguese and Italian, and from the start it points to the striped animal alone, so the animal sense is the core.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经葡萄牙语和意大利语进入英语，从一开始就只指这种有条纹的动物，所以「动物」是核心义项。

senses.title: Black and white stripes
senses.definition: a pattern or marking made of bold black and white bands
senses.definitionCN: 由醒目的黑白条带构成的图案或斑纹
senses.example: The carpet has a zebra design with wide stripes.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地毯是宽条纹的斑马图案。
senses.why: Because the stripes are the creature most striking feature, the animal name becomes a label for any bold black and white pattern.
senses.whyCN: 因为条纹是这种动物最醒目的特征，所以动物名被借来称呼任何醒目的黑白图案。

senses.title: The pedestrian crossing
senses.definition: a British name for a street crossing marked by broad white stripes
senses.definitionCN: 英国对这种以宽白条标出的人行横道的称法
senses.example: Look both ways before you use the zebra crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 过斑马线前先看清左右两边。
senses.why: A crossing painted with wide white bars looks like a giant set of stripes, so British English borrows the animal name for it.
senses.whyCN: 画着宽白条的过街处看起来像一大片条纹，所以英式英语借这个动物名来称呼它。

senses.title: Striped in appearance
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe something marked with black and white bands
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词前，形容某物带有黑白相间的条带
senses.example: She wore a zebra-striped scarf all winter.
senses.exampleCN: 整个冬天她都戴着一条斑马条纹的围巾。
senses.why: The animal name works as a modifier when the stripes are the point, giving us compounds like zebra-striped and zebra print.
senses.whyCN: 当重点在条纹上时，动物名就充当修饰语，形成 zebra-striped、zebra print 这样的复合形式。

intro.en: Zebra reached English in the seventeenth century through Portuguese or Italian, and its ultimate African source is uncertain.
intro.cn: zebra 在十七世纪经葡萄牙语或意大利语进入英语，其最终非洲来源不确定。

items.en: The ultimate origin is uncertain and may be linked to a Central African language such as Kongo.
items.cn: 最终来源不确定，可能与刚果语等中非语言有关。

items.en: Portuguese zebra and Italian zebra name the striped animal.
items.cn: 葡萄牙语 zebra 与意大利语 zebra 都指这种有条纹的动物。

items.en: English zebra is recorded in travel writing about Africa.
items.cn: 英语 zebra 见于十七世纪关于非洲的游记写作。

items.en: Zebra crossing is recorded from around 1949 because of the painted stripes.
items.cn: 由于路面绘有白条，zebra crossing 约在一九四九年见于记录。

items.en: The word spreads into patterns, fashion, and compound terms such as zebrafish and zebra crossing.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到图案、时尚以及 zebrafish、zebra crossing 等复合词中。

note.en: Zebra names one striped animal and, by extension, stripe patterns and the striped crossing used in British English.
note.cn: zebra 指一种有条纹的动物，又引申指条纹图案以及英式英语里的条纹斑马线。

entries.definition: more than one zebra
entries.definitionCN: 斑马的复数形式

entries.definition: an offspring of a zebra and a horse or donkey
entries.definitionCN: 斑马与马或驴的杂交后代

entries.definition: a small striped tropical fish used in science
entries.definitionCN: 一种有条纹的小型热带鱼，常用于科研

entries.definition: a long-eared farm animal related to the horse
entries.definitionCN: 驴（与马相近的动物）

entries.definition: a large four-legged animal often used for riding
entries.definitionCN: 马

entries.definition: a fast African animal with slender legs and horns
entries.definitionCN: 羚羊（非洲的快速草食动物）

normalIntro.en: Zebra links stripes, speed, and Africa, and its compounds carry the same image into language, science, and city streets.
normalIntro.cn: zebra 把条纹、速度与非洲联系在一起，它的复合词把这一意象带进语言、科学与城市街道。

normal.en: The plural is zebras, or zebra when talking about the herd as a whole.
normal.cn: 复数是 zebras；把整群当作集合时也说 a herd of zebra。

normal.en: Zebra crossing uses the striped look of the animal for the white bars painted on the road.
normal.cn: zebra crossing 借斑马的条纹外观来指路面画出的白条。

normal.en: It is not a zebra crossing in American English; Americans say crosswalk.
normal.cn: 美式英语不用 zebra crossing，美国人一般说 crosswalk。

normal.en: Zebrafish is a compound with fish, borrowed from the striped little fish.
normal.cn: zebrafish 与 fish 复合，借这种小鱼身上的条纹得名。

normal.en: Zebra finch names a small bird with striped plumage, showing the pattern again.
normal.cn: zebra finch 指羽毛有条纹的小鸟，再次体现了条纹这一特征。

abstract.en: Picture black and white bars running across a horse from nose to tail.
abstract.cn: 想象黑白条带像横纹一样从头到尾布满马身。

abstract.en: Imagine walking on wide white bars painted across a busy street.
abstract.cn: 想象走在繁忙街道上画出的宽白条上。

abstract.en: Think of a fashion show where a striped scarf crosses the stage.
abstract.cn: 想象时装秀上一条黑白条纹围巾横过舞台。

examples.en: Each zebra has its own stripe pattern, like a fingerprint.
examples.cn: 每匹斑马的条纹图案都不同，就像指纹一样。

examples.en: The children waited at the zebra crossing for the light.
examples.cn: 孩子们在斑马线处等红灯。

examples.en: Her dress had a bold zebra pattern.
examples.cn: 她的连衣裙是醒目的黑白斑马纹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泽布拉」——在泽水边拉起一道黑白布拉条，就是斑马身上的条纹；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定：一般认为经葡萄牙语 zebra 或意大利语 zebra 传入，可能是非洲语言借词，常见的一种说法是与刚果语家族有关，但无定论；英语于十七世纪记录 zebra，核心义「黑白条纹的非洲野马」。

sensesIntro.en: Zebra starts as the striped African horse, then lends its stripes to patterns and, in British English, to the white-barred street crossing.
sensesIntro.cn: zebra 先是黑白条纹的非洲野马，再把条纹借给图案，并在英式英语中借给画白条的过街处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wild African horse covered in black and white stripes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一匹浑身布满黑白条纹的非洲野马。

branches.en: The animal itself is the core sense.
branches.cn: 动物本身是核心义项。

branches.en: The stripes become a general pattern.
branches.cn: 条纹变成一种通用图案。

branches.en: British streets borrow the name for the striped crossing.
branches.cn: 英国街道借这个词称呼条纹人行道。

branches.en: The herd and the pattern both come from the visual impact of stripes.
branches.cn: 兽群与图案都源于条纹带来的视觉冲击。

branches.en: Stripe patterns become adjectives and compounds through a single image.
branches.cn: 条纹图案经由同一意象变成形容词与复合词。

intro.en: Zebra has no productive Latin affixes, so the word builds English compounds such as zebrafish and zebra crossing instead.
intro.cn: zebra 没有可再产出的拉丁词缀，英语主要靠复合构词形成 zebrafish、zebra crossing 等形式。

latinIntro.en: The word family has no clear Latin root; zebra is usually treated as a Portuguese or Italian borrowing from African sources.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族没有清晰的拉丁词根；zebra 一般被看作葡萄牙语或意大利语从非洲语言借来的词。

items.example: Zebra is the base noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: zebra 是这个词族的基础名词。

items.example: The plural form adds -s.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式加 -s。

items.example: The compound uses the striped look of the animal.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词借用了动物的条纹外观。

items.meaning: marked with black and white stripes
items.example: The adjective is joined with a hyphen.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词用连字符连接。

items.example: Fish is the second element.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分是 fish。

items.example: The suffix -oid means resembling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -oid 意为「像……的」。

items.meaning: a plant named for zebra stripes
items.meaningCN: 因斑马条纹而得名的植物
items.example: Zebrina borrows the striped look for a plant name.
items.exampleCN: zebrina 借条纹外观为植物命名。

items.example: Finch is the second element.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分是 finch。

definition_zh: 天顶；顶点；巅峰；最高点；鼎盛时期
definition_en: the highest point directly above an observer, or the greatest height of something
core_image: 抬头望天，太阳或星星正停在头顶正上方那一点
scene: 摄影师等待着太阳升到天顶，那一刻的影子最短，光线也最亮。At noon the sun reached its zenith and the shadows shrank to almost nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 zenith 是「天顶」的意思（第 1 个义项：观测者头顶正上方的那一点）；句意：正午时太阳到达天顶，影子几乎缩到没有了。

pos.zh: 天顶（观测者头顶正上方的天球点）
鼎盛时期（事业或权力的全盛阶段）

derivatives.zh: 由 zenith 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「天顶的；从天顶方向的」
由 zenith 与 distance 复合而成，义为「天顶距」，即天体与天顶的角距

senses.title: The overhead point
senses.definition: the point in the sky directly above an observer, opposite to the horizon point below
senses.definitionCN: 观测者正头顶上方的天球点，与脚下的地平点相对
senses.example: The star passed through the zenith at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗星在午夜经过天顶。
senses.why: The Arabic word samt means path or direction, and the astronomical point straight overhead is the earliest and still the most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 阿拉伯语 samt 意为「路径、方向」，正头顶的那个天文点是这个词最早、也最字面的义项。

senses.title: The highest point
senses.definition: the highest or most powerful point that something reaches
senses.definitionCN: 某事物所能达到的最高点或最强点
senses.example: The demand for those phones was at its zenith last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年那几款手机的需求达到了最高点。
senses.why: Since the zenith is the top of the sky, any rise measured on a scale finishes there, so the word names the highest point more generally.
senses.whyCN: 既然天顶是天空的最高处，任何按刻度上升的过程都会在那里到头，于是这个词一般化地指最高点。

senses.title: The peak of success
senses.definition: the moment when a person or thing is at its most successful or glorious
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某事物最为成功或最辉煌的时刻
senses.example: The empire was at its zenith under that queen.
senses.exampleCN: 那个帝国在那位女王治下处于鼎盛时期。
senses.why: A career or a nation also rises to a top and then falls, so the spatial zenith becomes a picture of success at its peak.
senses.whyCN: 事业或国家同样有升到顶点再下落的过程，于是空间上的天顶成为「成功巅峰」的画面。

intro.en: Zenith is a medieval Latin rendering of Arabic samt, path or direction, usually shortened from a phrase about the path over the head.
intro.cn: zenith 是中世纪拉丁语对阿拉伯语 samt（路径、方向）的转写，通常认为出自指「头顶上方路径」的词组缩写。

items.en: Arabic samt means path or direction, used in astronomy and timekeeping.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 samt 意为路径或方向，用于天文与计时。

items.en: The phrase samt al-ras means the direction over the head.
items.cn: 词组 samt al-ras 意为「头顶上方的方向」。

items.en: Medieval Latin writers turned the phrase into cenit, which later becomes zenith.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语作者把这个词组改写成 cenit，后来又变成 zenith。

items.en: Old Spanish cenit or zenit mirrors the same astronomical term.
items.cn: 古西班牙语 cenit 或 zenit 是同一天文术语的对应形式。

items.en: English adopts the astronomical sense first, and the figurative top sense follows.
items.cn: 英语先采用天文义，随后发展出比喻性的「最高点」。

note.en: Zenith names the top of the sky and, by analogy, the highest point of anything; it sits beside words for peaks and their opposites.
note.cn: zenith 指天空的最高处，并以此类比任何事物的最高点；它与表示「巅峰」及反义的词相邻。

entries.definition: relating to the point overhead
entries.definitionCN: 天顶的；来自天顶方向的

entries.definition: an angle used to locate a point on the horizon
entries.definitionCN: 方位角；仅拼写相似，词源与 zenith 同为阿拉伯语 samt 系统

entries.definition: the point in the sky directly below an observer
entries.definitionCN: 天底（与天顶相对的点）

entries.definition: the highest point or level
entries.definitionCN: 顶峰；最高水平

entries.definition: the top of a mountain or of a career
entries.definitionCN: 山顶；巅峰

entries.definition: the highest point of achievement
entries.definitionCN: 顶点；极致

normalIntro.en: Zenith holds an Arabic image of direction overhead, shared with nadir and azimuth, and it turns that sky-high point into a measure of success.
normalIntro.cn: zenith 带着阿拉伯语「头顶方向」的意象，与 nadir、azimuth 同属一套天空坐标，并把天空最高处变成衡量成功的尺度。

normal.en: Zenith and nadir are opposites: one is straight up, the other straight down.
normal.cn: zenith 与 nadir 相对：一个正上方，一个正下方。

normal.en: Azimuth shares the Arabic root samt, though its modern sense is an angle on the horizon.
normal.cn: azimuth 与它同出阿拉伯语词根 samt，但现代义是地平上的角度。

normal.en: The adjective zenithal adds -al, meaning at or from the zenith.
normal.cn: 形容词 zenithal 加后缀 -al，表示「天顶的、来自天顶的」。

normal.en: The phrase at its zenith means at the most successful moment.
normal.cn: at its zenith 意为「处于鼎盛时期」。

normal.en: The compound zenith distance adds distance for the angle between the zenith and a star.
normal.cn: 复合词 zenith distance 加 distance，指天顶与某颗星的夹角。

abstract.en: Picture a sun directly over your head at noon, the shortest shadow of the day.
abstract.cn: 想象正午太阳就在头顶正上方，地上的影子最短。

abstract.en: Imagine a mountain path that ends at the very top, with no more climbing left.
abstract.cn: 想象一条山路走到最高处，再没有可攀登的了。

abstract.en: Think of a career rising like a rocket and then staying at its highest shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象事业像火箭一样上升，最后停在其最高的那层架子上。

examples.en: The climbers reached the zenith of their career after ten years.
examples.cn: 攀登者在十年后达到了事业巅峰。

examples.en: The observatory measures the zenith angle of each star.
examples.cn: 天文台测量每颗星的天顶角。

examples.en: Silk trade was at its zenith under that dynasty.
examples.cn: 丝绸之路在那个王朝时期处于鼎盛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「立顶」——立在这座山的顶端，就是最高点；也可以想「真顶」，真真正正到了顶。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源于阿拉伯语 samt（路径、方向），常出自词组 samt al-ras（头顶上方的方向）的缩写，经中世纪拉丁语 cenit 转写，英语作 zenith；核心义「观测者头顶正上方的天球点」。

sensesIntro.en: Zenith begins as the sky point overhead, then becomes the highest point of any rise, and finally the peak of success or glory.
sensesIntro.cn: zenith 先指头顶正上方的天球点，再指任何上升过程的最高点，最后指成功或荣耀的巅峰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a point in the sky straight above your head.
core.cn: 核心意象：你头顶正上方的那一点天空。

branches.en: The astronomical point overhead is the literal core.
branches.cn: 头顶的天文点是字面核心义。

branches.en: Any scale of rise borrows the top of the sky.
branches.cn: 任何上升的刻度都借用天空的最高处。

branches.en: Success at its highest becomes the figurative zenith.
branches.cn: 成功的最高处成为比喻的巅峰。

branches.en: Both astronomy and everyday speech use a single picture of straight up.
branches.cn: 天文学与日常说法共用「正上方」这一画面。

branches.en: A high point in supply or fame is both a measurement and a glory.
branches.cn: 供应量或名声的高点既是测量值也是荣耀。

intro.en: Zenith is a borrowed Arabic term with little internal affixation; English adds suffixes such as -al and compounds such as zenith distance.
intro.cn: zenith 是借来的阿拉伯语术语，内部词缀很少；英语为它加 -al 等后缀，并构成 zenith distance 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: The term passed through medieval Latin cenit and Old Spanish cenit, which shaped the final spelling.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经过中世纪拉丁语 cenit 与古西班牙语 cenit，最终定形为今天的拼写。

items.example: Samt gives the term its sense of direction.
items.exampleCN: samt 为这个词提供「方向」的含义。

items.example: Cenit is the Latin rendering of the Arabic phrase.
items.exampleCN: cenit 是阿拉伯语词组在拉丁语中的转写。

items.example: Zenith is the base noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: zenith 是这个词族的基础名词。

items.example: The plural adds -s.
items.exampleCN: 复数加 -s。

items.example: The suffix -al forms zenithal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 zenithal。

items.example: Zenithal describes a position overhead.
items.exampleCN: zenithal 描述头顶上的位置。

items.meaning: the final sound of the borrowed word
items.example: The ending -th follows the Latin and Spanish spelling.
items.exampleCN: 结尾 -th 沿袭了拉丁语与西班牙语的拼法。

items.meaning: the angle from the zenith to a point
items.example: Distance is the second element.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分是 distance。

definition_zh: 热情；兴致；柑橘外皮；调味；增添风味之物
definition_en: great enthusiasm and energy, or the thin outer skin of a citrus fruit used to flavour food
core_image: 擦在柠檬上的小刨刀，刨出一缕缕油亮的黄色表皮
scene: 厨房里飘来一股清新的香气。The cook grated the zest of a lemon into the cake batter.
sceneCN: 这里 zest 是「柑橘外皮」（第 2 个义项：擦成细丝、用来增香的果皮）；句意：厨师把柠檬外皮擦进蛋糕面糊里。

pos.zh: 热情；兴致；柑橘外皮；风味

collocations.phrase: grate the zest of an orange

derivatives.zh: 由 zest 加 -ful 构成，意为「热情洋溢的；有滋味的」
由 zest 加 -y 构成，意为「辛辣开胃的；活泼有趣的」
由 zest 加 -less 构成，意为「没有热情、寡淡无味的」
由 zesty 加 -ly 构成，意为「起劲地、劲头十足地」

senses.title: Enthusiastic energy
senses.definition: lively interest and eager enjoyment of what one is doing
senses.definitionCN: 对所做的事情怀有浓厚的兴趣和热切的享受
senses.example: She attacked the new project with zest.
senses.exampleCN: 她满怀热情地投入这个新项目。
senses.why: The core image is grated peel that tingles on the tongue, so the word was borrowed for a sharpening of appetite that makes people act eagerly.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是擦成细丝的果皮在舌上微微刺激，于是被借指让人胃口大开的劲头，使人做事兴致勃勃。

senses.title: Citrus peel used for flavour
senses.definition: the coloured outer layer of a citrus fruit, grated or cut for flavouring
senses.definitionCN: 柑橘类水果有颜色的外层表皮，常擦丝或切条用来调味
senses.example: A spoonful of orange zest lifts the sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 一勺橙皮屑就能让酱汁格外出彩。
senses.why: This is the oldest concrete sense: a French cook took the peel, zeste, and turned it into a word of its own.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早就有的具体义项：法语里把果皮叫作 zeste，后来独立成一个英语词。

senses.title: Something that adds flavour
senses.definition: a substance that is the skin of a fruit used to add flavour to food
senses.definitionCN: 取自某种水果表皮、用来给食物加味的材料
senses.example: The recipe calls for a small piece of lemon zest.
senses.exampleCN: 这个食谱需要一小片柠檬皮。
senses.why: Once the peel was seen as an ingredient, any small piece of skin added for flavour could be called a zest.
senses.whyCN: 当果皮被视为一种配料后，任何为增味而加入的一小片表皮都可称为 zest。

senses.title: A quality that adds interest
senses.definition: an appealing or exciting quality that makes something more interesting
senses.definitionCN: 使事物更有趣、更吸引人的那种特质
senses.example: The stories give a real zest to the tour.
senses.exampleCN: 这些故事让旅程真正有了趣味。
senses.why: The same sharpening idea moves from food to experience: anything that makes an occasion livelier gives it zest.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「提味」观念从食物移到体验：凡是让场合活起来、变得有趣的东西，都是在给它添味。

senses.title: Eagerness for a thing
senses.definition: keen interest shown in an activity or in life itself
senses.definitionCN: 对某种活动或对生活本身表现出的浓烈兴趣
senses.example: He has a zest for life that is hard to resist.
senses.exampleCN: 他对生活的那股热情让人难以抗拒。
senses.why: Hunger was once believed to be sharpened by the peel, so zest came to mean a keen appetite for an object.
senses.whyCN: 古人相信果皮能刺激食欲，因此 zest 又表示对某事物强烈的胃口。

senses.title: To add flavour to
senses.definition: to give extra flavour to food or extra liveliness to something
senses.definitionCN: 为食物添味道，或为某事增添生气
senses.example: A squeeze of lemon zests up the grilled fish.
senses.exampleCN: 挤一点柠檬汁就能让烤鱼更有滋味。
senses.why: A sense of appetite opened the way to a verb: to zest something is to give it that appetising edge.
senses.whyCN: 与食欲相关的这层意思又发展出动词用法：to zest 就是给某物加上开胃的边角。

intro.en: Zest comes from French zeste, the peel of a citrus fruit; an older Latin family is sometimes suggested but is not certain.
intro.cn: zest 来自法语 zeste，指柑橘类果皮；有时会被追溯到更古老的拉丁语同族词，但尚无定论。

items.en: Some scholars look for a link to Latin schistus, a cleft stone, a word borrowed from Greek.
items.cn: 有学者试图把它和拉丁语 schistus（劈开的石头，源自希腊语）联系起来。

items.en: The noun zeste names the thin peel of a citrus fruit.
items.cn: 古法语名词 zeste 指柑橘的薄皮。

items.en: French cooks use zest and the verb zester to mean peel and to strip peel.
items.cn: 法语中的 zest 与动词 zester 已有剥皮、擦皮之意。

items.en: English borrows zest as the name of the flavouring peel, especially of oranges and lemons.
items.cn: 英语借入 zest，特指橙、柠檬等果皮。

items.en: The sense extends from a little piece of peel to anything that heightens flavour or interest.
items.cn: 词义从一小片果皮扩展到一切能提味、增趣之物。

items.en: Modern English makes it stand for keen appetite: having a zest for life.
items.cn: 现代英语让它表示强烈的胃口：对生活的热情。

note.en: Zest is an appetite word borrowed from the kitchen, close to enthusiasm words and to citrus peel terms.
note.cn: zest 是从厨房借来的「开胃」词，与表示热情的词以及柑橘表皮类词相邻。

entries.definition: full of eager energy
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生：由 zest 加 -ful 构成，意为「热情洋溢的」

entries.definition: tasting sharp and fresh, or lively
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生：加了 -y 的形容词，意为「开胃的；活泼的」

entries.definition: without enthusiasm or flavour
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生：加 -less 构成，意为「没有热情的」

entries.definition: strong excitement and interest
entries.definitionCN: 近义：强烈的兴奋和兴趣，偏正式

entries.definition: the skin of a fruit or vegetable
entries.definitionCN: 近义：果皮或菜皮，范围更宽，但不特指调味

entries.definition: eager enjoyment of doing something
entries.definitionCN: 近义：做事的酣畅劲头，多与吃东西、投入某事有关

normalIntro.en: Zest began as kitchen peel and grew into eager energy, so both memories should smell of citrus.
normalIntro.cn: zest 从厨房果皮长成一股劲头，两种记忆都该带柑橘香气。

normal.en: Lemon zest is grated peel used in baking.
normal.cn: lemon zest 是烘焙用的擦细柠檬皮。

normal.en: Something done with zest is done eagerly.
normal.cn: with zest 做的事就是带着劲头做的。

normal.en: A person with a zest for life enjoys living.
normal.cn: 有生活热情的人，享受活着这件事。

normal.en: To add zest to a party is to make it livelier.
normal.cn: add zest to a party 就是给聚会添彩。

normal.en: Compare peel as a general word: zest is a thin flavouring peel.
normal.cn: 对比 peel：peel 泛指果皮，zest 专指调味的薄皮。

abstract.en: Picture a chef shredding bright yellow peel while humming.
abstract.cn: 想象厨师一边哼歌一边擦出鲜黄的果皮细丝。

abstract.en: See a lemon turning in a grater and throwing out curls of skin.
abstract.cn: 想象柠檬在擦板上转动，卷出丝丝表皮。

abstract.en: Think of a bland dish and one pinch of peel that wakes it up.
abstract.cn: 想象一道寡淡的菜，靠一小撮果皮就醒了过来。

examples.en: He plays the piano with great zest.
examples.cn: 他弹钢琴时劲头十足。

examples.en: Add a teaspoon of lime zest to the dressing.
examples.cn: 往调味汁里加一茶匙青柠皮。

examples.en: Her travels gave her a fresh zest for studying languages.
examples.cn: 旅行让她重新燃起了学语言的兴致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「柑丝特」——柑橘擦出一把细丝，皮丝提味、人生提神；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 法语 zeste（柑橘果皮）→ 英语 zest；更早的拉丁语同族属「一般认为」的猜测，未确证。核心义「擦下来的一小片提味果皮」。

sensesIntro.en: Zest moves from the physical peel of a citrus fruit to the flavour it gives, and finally to the keen energy found in a person.
sensesIntro.cn: zest 从实物的柑橘表皮，延伸到它带来的味道，最后落到一个人身上那股旺盛的劲头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: curls of grated citrus peel that are pungent and fresh.
core.cn: 核心意象：擦下来的一缕缕柑橘果皮，辛香清新。

branches.en: The physical peel is the concrete starting point.
branches.cn: 实物的柑橘表皮是具体起点。

branches.en: The peel becomes an ingredient that spices up a dish or an occasion.
branches.cn: 果皮变成配料，给菜肴或场合提味。

branches.en: A sharpened appetite turns into eager interest in a task or in life.
branches.cn: 胃口被刺激，转为对事情或生活的热烈兴趣。

branches.en: The flavour idea supports the verb meaning to add zest.
branches.cn: 提味这一层意思支撑了动词「增添风味」。

branches.en: Both the peel and the eager person are described as fresh and sharp.
branches.cn: 果皮和热情的人都被形容为清新、锐利。

intro.en: Zest is a borrowed French noun; English builds zestful, zesty, and zestless around it.
intro.cn: zest 是从法语借来的名词，英语围绕它构成 zestful、zesty 与 zestless。

latinIntro.en: The Latin link to schistus is only a suggestion; the reliable period of record begins in French.
latinIntro.cn: 与拉丁语 schistus 的联系只是推测，可靠的记载从法语开始。

items.example: From the French noun zeste the English noun was formed.
items.exampleCN: 英语 zest 由法语名词 zeste 借来。

items.example: The verb zester meant to strip peel.
items.exampleCN: 动词 zester 意为剥去果皮。

items.example: The first English sense was the flavouring peel.
items.exampleCN: 最早英语义项是调味的果皮。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms zestful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 构成 zestful。

items.example: Zestful describes a lively person.
items.exampleCN: zestful 形容活力充沛的人。

items.example: The suffix -y forms zesty.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 zesty。

items.example: Zesty sauce tastes of citrus.
items.exampleCN: zesty 酱汁有柑橘味。

items.example: The suffix -less forms zestless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 zestless。

items.example: Zestless food lacks any tang.
items.exampleCN: zestless 食物毫无风味。

items.example: The suffix -er forms the kitchen tool called zester.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成厨房工具 zester。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 劈开的石头（源自希腊语），与 zeste 的联系仅为推测

definition_en: a bluish white metal used to protect iron from rusting and in making brass
core_image: 灰色铁栏被浸入银色熔液，抽出时裹上一层发亮的薄壳
scene: 桥梁的护栏常年淋雨却不见锈迹。The steel railing is protected by a thin coat of zinc.
sceneCN: 这里 zinc 是「锌」（第 1 个义项：一种化学元素与金属）；句意：这道钢栏杆靠一层薄薄的锌来保护。

forms.label: 复数形式（少见，指锌矿石）

derivatives.zh: 由 zinc 加 -ous 构成，意为「含锌的、锌的」
由 zinc 加 -ate 构成，指「锌酸盐」
由 zinc 加 -ate 与 -ed 构成，指「镀过锌的」

senses.title: The element zinc
senses.definition: a chemical element, a bluish white and fairly reactive metal
senses.definitionCN: 一种化学元素，属于偏蓝的白色金属，活性较强
senses.example: Zinc reacts more readily with acids than iron does.
senses.exampleCN: 锌比铁更容易与酸发生反应。
senses.why: The word entered science as a name borrowed from German, and modern chemistry fixed it on one element.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初作为从德语借来的名字进入科学，现代化学把它固定为一个元素。

senses.title: The metal as a material
senses.definition: the metal zinc as a material, for example sheets used in roofs and batteries
senses.definitionCN: 作为材料的锌，例如用于屋顶与电池的锌板
senses.example: The shed roof is made of curved zinc.
senses.exampleCN: 棚屋屋顶用弯曲的锌板做成。
senses.why: A pure substance named in chemistry also names the goods and sheets made from it.
senses.whyCN: 化学上命名的纯物质，也会指用它所制成的板材和货品。

senses.title: To coat with zinc
senses.definition: to cover iron or steel with zinc to stop it rusting
senses.definitionCN: 在铁或钢表面覆上锌，以防生锈
senses.example: Workers zinc the bolts before they go into the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 螺栓在装上桥之前要由工人镀锌。
senses.why: Because the metal protects other metals, naming it also gave a verb for that protective act.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种金属能保护别的金属，所以用它命名的动词也表示这种保护动作。

senses.title: A nutrient for the body
senses.definition: zinc as a nutrient needed in small amounts for health
senses.definitionCN: 作为人体需要少量摄入的营养素
senses.example: Doctors linked her slow healing to low zinc in her diet.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把她伤口愈合慢归因于饮食中缺锌。
senses.why: Once the metal was known to be vital in tiny doses, the word spread from factories to medicine.
senses.whyCN: 当人们知道这种金属在微量下不可或缺，这个词就从工厂走进医学。

senses.title: Part of brass
senses.definition: the metal combined with copper to make brass
senses.definitionCN: 与铜熔合制成黄铜的那种金属
senses.example: Brass is almost a third zinc.
senses.exampleCN: 黄铜中锌的成分接近三分之一。
senses.why: Zinc was first prized in Europe as the secret ingredient that turned copper into gold coloured brass.
senses.whyCN: 锌在欧洲最早受重视，是因为它是把铜变成金色的黄铜的神秘配料。

intro.en: Zinc is first recorded in German, probably from an older Persian or Arabic word; the exact origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: zinc 最早见于德语，很可能源自更早的波斯语或阿拉伯语；确切来源不确定。

items.en: A word like sing or chang is thought to mean stone or ore, but this is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为类似 sing 或 chang 的词意为石头、矿石，但依据不足。

items.en: Arabic writers knew the grey ore, and a related name travelled into European languages.
items.cn: 阿拉伯文献里已有这种灰色矿石的记载，相关名称随后传入欧洲语言。

items.en: German miners and writers use zink for the bluish metal and its ore.
items.cn: 十六世纪的德语矿工与写作者用 zink 指这种偏蓝的金属及其矿石。

items.en: English borrows zinc, often describing the smoky metal sold to brass makers.
items.cn: 英语借入 zinc，常用来描述卖给黄铜匠人的这种冒烟金属。

items.en: Chemistry lists zinc as an element, and industry spreads it over more iron surfaces.
items.cn: 化学把锌列为元素，工业让它覆盖越来越多的铁件表面。

items.en: Zinc also names a nutrient and a common material for roofs and batteries.
items.cn: 现代英语中 zinc 还指一种营养素，以及屋顶和电池的常见材料。

note.en: Zinc is a metal name; it resembles names of other metals and other words that share the zinc stem.
note.cn: zinc 是金属名称，与其它金属名称以及带 zinc 词干的词相邻。

entries.definition: coated with zinc
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生：加 -ed 的形容词，意为「镀过锌的」

entries.definition: made of or containing zinc
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生：加 -ous 构成，意为「锌的、含锌的」

entries.definition: a salt or compound containing zinc
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生：加 -ate 构成，指锌酸盐类化合物

entries.definition: to coat iron with zinc
entries.definitionCN: 近义：给铁镀锌，常与 zinc 出现在同一语境

entries.definition: an alloy of copper and zinc
entries.definitionCN: 相关：铜与锌的合金

entries.definition: a heavy soft grey metal
entries.definitionCN: 同类：铅，另一种常见软金属，常与锌成对出现

normalIntro.en: Zinc is a short metallic word; the memories should hang on coating iron, brass, and the body.
normalIntro.cn: zinc 是个短小的金属词，记忆应挂在镀铁、黄铜与身体三件事上。

normal.en: A zinc coating stops steel from rusting.
normal.cn: 锌层能防止钢材生锈。

normal.en: Brass is made of copper and zinc.
normal.cn: 黄铜由铜和锌制成。

normal.en: Zinc oxide is the white cream in a sun lotion.
normal.cn: 氧化锌是防晒霜里的白色膏体。

normal.en: A zinc deficiency can slow healing.
normal.cn: 缺锌会让伤口愈合变慢。

normal.en: Compare copper, a warmer metal, to see the family of metal names.
normal.cn: 对比同属金属名的 copper，它更偏暖色，可帮助记住这一族词。

abstract.en: Picture gray iron bars dipped into a silver bath.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色铁条被浸入银色熔液。

abstract.en: Hear the ringing sound of a zinc roof in the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨点打在锌皮屋顶上的脆响。

abstract.en: See a brass doorknob shining because zinc is mixed into the copper.
abstract.cn: 想象铜里混进锌后，门把手泛出黄铜的光。

examples.en: The metal fence is coated with zinc to keep it from rusting.
examples.cn: 这道铁栅栏镀了锌，以防锈蚀。

examples.en: Zinc and copper are melted together to make brass.
examples.cn: 锌与铜熔在一起制成黄铜。

examples.en: The doctor advised a diet rich in zinc.
examples.cn: 医生建议多吃含锌丰富的食物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「锌」读起来像「新」——栏杆镀上锌，就崭新发亮不生锈；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 德语 zink（16 世纪，偏蓝的金属）→ 英语 zinc；更早多见于波斯语、阿拉伯语的说法，确切形式不确定。核心义「一种色偏蓝白、能护住铁的金属」。

sensesIntro.en: Zinc names the element, then the metal as stock, the act of coating iron with it, its use inside the body, and its role in brass.
sensesIntro.cn: zinc 先指一种元素，再指作为材料的金属、用它镀铁的动作、它在人体里的作用以及它在黄铜中的地位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey bar dipped into a silver bath and pulled out coated.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰色铁条浸入银色熔液，取出时已披上一层薄壳。

branches.en: Chemistry gives the element its name.
branches.cn: 化学为这种元素定名。

branches.en: The metal appears as sheets and other goods.
branches.cn: 这种金属以板材等成品形态出现。

branches.en: Protecting iron is zinc at work.
branches.cn: 保护钢铁就是锌在起作用。

branches.en: The same metal becomes a tiny daily need for the body.
branches.cn: 同一种金属成为身体每日所需的微量成分。

branches.en: Element and alloy share the metal that gives brass its colour.
branches.cn: 元素与合金共享同一种金属，正是它让黄铜有了颜色。

intro.en: Zinc is a borrowed metal name; English forms zinced, zincous, and zincate around it.
intro.cn: zinc 是借来的金属名，英语围绕它构成 zinced、zincous 与 zincate。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor: the word comes through German from a Persian or Arabic name whose form is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先：它经由德语来自波斯语或阿拉伯语的名称，具体形式不确定。

items.example: German zink is the source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 德语 zink 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: Zinc names the metal and the element.
items.exampleCN: zinc 既指这种金属，也指这个元素。

items.example: The verb zinc means to coat iron.
items.exampleCN: 动词 zinc 意为给铁镀锌。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms zinced.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 zinced。

items.example: Zinced nails resist rust.
items.exampleCN: zinced 钉子不易生锈。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms zincous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 zincous。

items.example: Zincous ores are mined in several regions.
items.exampleCN: zincous 矿石在多个地区开采。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms zincate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 构成 zincate。

items.example: Zincate appears in plating baths.
items.exampleCN: zincate 用于电镀液。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms zincing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 zincing。

definition_zh: 僵尸；无精打采的人；行尸走肉般的状态；僵死的旧观念
definition_en: a dead body brought back to life in folklore, or a lifeless, exhausted person
core_image: 拖着脚走在黑暗港口的失魂人影，眼神空洞、动作僵直
scene: 加勒比海的渔村夜里流传着怪谈。Some villagers still tell old stories of zombies rising from their graves.
sceneCN: 这里 zombie 是「僵尸」（第 1 个义项：传说中复活的死人）；句意：一些村民至今还在讲僵尸从坟里爬出来的老故事。

pos.zh: 僵尸；迟钝的人；行尸走肉般的状态

derivatives.zh: 由 zombie 加 -ify 构成，意为「使变得麻木迟钝；把……变成僵尸」
由 zombify 加 -ation 构成，意为「麻木化；僵尸化」
由 zombify 加 -ed 构成，意为「变成行尸走肉的；死气沉沉的」
由 zombie 去掉词尾 e 加 -y 构成的早期变体，意为「僵尸般的」

senses.title: A dead body walking again
senses.definition: in folklore and film, a dead person who has been brought back to life as a walking body
senses.definitionCN: 在民间传说与影视中，被复活后仍以肉体行走的死人
senses.example: The film opens with a zombie rising from a shallow grave.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影以一个僵尸从浅坟里爬出来开场。
senses.why: This is the source sense, brought to the West from Caribbean, especially Haitian, belief and then carried by horror films.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：它从加勒比地区尤其是海地的信仰中传来，再由恐怖片推动流行。

senses.title: A lifeless person
senses.titleCN: 无精打采的人；迟钝的人
senses.definition: a person who seems to have no energy or will of their own
senses.definitionCN: 显得没有活力、也没有自主意志的人
senses.example: I was a zombie after three night shifts.
senses.exampleCN: 连上三个夜班后我像个行尸走肉。
senses.why: Since a zombie in folklore has no mind of its own, the word naturally names someone worn out and mechanical.
senses.whyCN: 传说中的僵尸没有自己的心智，因此这个词自然地用来指疲惫麻木、只会机械行动的人。

senses.title: A machine that will not stop
senses.titleCN: 失控的运行程序；停不下来的机制
senses.definition: a process or system that keeps going although it no longer does anything useful
senses.definitionCN: 已不再产生用处却仍在持续运行的程序或系统
senses.example: The old server was full of zombies nobody dared to switch off.
senses.exampleCN: 那台老服务器上全是不敢关掉的僵尸进程。
senses.why: A body without life resembles a program without a purpose, so computing borrowed the word for systems that will not die.
senses.whyCN: 没有生命却还在动的躯体，很像没有意义却仍在运行的程序，于是计算机领域借用了这个词。

senses.title: A word slowly dying out
senses.definition: an old word or idea that survives in memory but no longer lives in language
senses.definitionCN: 仍留在记忆里、却已不在语言中真正使用的旧词或旧观念
senses.example: Critics call that old word a zombie, kept alive only in footnotes.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者把那个旧词叫作僵尸词，只在脚注里勉强存活。
senses.why: Literary critics took the walking corpse as an image: a word that is remembered but no longer used is a zombie.
senses.whyCN: 文学评论家借用了行走尸体的意象：能被记住却不再被使用的词，就是僵尸词。

senses.title: Something kept alive artificially
senses.definition: a company, rule, or custom that survives only through outside support
senses.definitionCN: 只靠外部扶持才勉强存续的公司、规定或习俗
senses.example: Regulators want to close the zombie bank before losses grow.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构想在这家僵而不死的银行损失扩大前把它关掉。
senses.why: The film zombie is kept moving by outside force, and the business sense copies that idea of artificial survival.
senses.whyCN: 电影里的僵尸靠外力撑起身子，金融领域借用了这种「人为续命」的意思。

intro.en: Zombie comes from the Caribbean, most likely through Haiti and African languages spoken by enslaved people; the exact source is uncertain.
intro.cn: zombie 源自加勒比地区，很可能经由海地以及被奴役者所说的非洲语言传入；确切来源不确定。

items.en: Languages such as Kikongo have words like nzambi, meaning god or spirit, often suggested as the source.
items.cn: 一般认为刚果语等班图语族中的 nzambi（神、神灵）是来源之一，但未见定论。

items.en: In Haiti zombie names a body said to be raised by sorcery and worked as a slave.
items.cn: 在海地克里奥尔语中，zombie 指据说被巫术复活的、被驱使为奴的尸体。

items.en: The form zumbi is also used, mainly in the Americas, and may have influenced the spelling.
items.cn: 美洲也有 zumbi 这一形式，可能影响了拼写。

items.en: Early English reports of Haiti bring the word in, often with an exotic tone.
items.cn: 十九世纪关于海地的英语记述把它带入英语，常带异国色彩。

items.en: Horror films make zombie a common word for the walking dead.
items.cn: 二十世纪的恐怖电影让 zombie 成为指「活死人」的普通词。

items.en: Computing, finance, and criticism reuse it for things that keep going without life.
items.cn: 计算机、金融与评论领域借它指那些没有生命却仍在运转的事物。

note.en: Zombie is a Caribbean walker of the dead; it sits beside related undead words and beside words built on its stem.
note.cn: zombie 是来自加勒比的「行走的死者」，与相关的亡灵词以及带 zombie 词干的词相邻。

entries.definition: more than one zombie
entries.definitionCN: 同根形式：复数，直接加 s

entries.definition: to make someone lifeless or dull
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生：加 -ify 的动词，意为「使麻木迟钝」

entries.definition: the process of becoming like a zombie
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生：加 -ation 的名词，意为「僵尸化」

entries.definition: the spirit of a dead person
entries.definitionCN: 临近义场：鬼魂，没有肉体

entries.definition: a dead body
entries.definitionCN: 临近义场：尸体，不会走动

entries.definition: a preserved body of the ancient dead
entries.definitionCN: 同类：木乃伊，被保存起来的古尸

normalIntro.en: Zombie is a Caribbean word for the walking dead; the memories should link Haiti, film, and the dull exhausted person.
normalIntro.cn: zombie 是加勒比的「活死人」一词，记忆应串起海地、电影与麻木疲惫的人。

normal.en: A zombie film shows the dead walking again.
normal.cn: zombie film 演的是死者又一次行走。

normal.en: After no sleep, people walk like zombies.
normal.cn: 没睡觉的人走路像僵尸。

normal.en: A zombie company survives only on rescue money.
normal.cn: zombie company 只靠救助资金活着。

normal.en: The plural is zombie with an s: zombies.
normal.cn: 复数是直接在 zombie 后加 s：zombies。

normal.en: Compare ghost and corpse: a zombie has a body but no life.
normal.cn: 对比 ghost 与 corpse：僵尸有身体却没有生命。

abstract.en: Picture a figure dragging one foot after the other in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一个身影在黑暗中一只脚拖着另一只脚往前挪。

abstract.en: Think of a screen glowing at midnight and a person staring at it blankly.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜屏幕发亮，一个人呆呆盯着它。

abstract.en: See a program that keeps running with nothing left to do.
abstract.cn: 想象一个程序空转着、却早已没什么可做。

examples.en: The zombie walked slowly across the empty street.
examples.cn: 那个僵尸缓慢地走过空荡的街道。

examples.en: He felt like a zombie after two days without sleep.
examples.cn: 两天没睡，他觉得自己像具行尸走肉。

examples.en: Economists warn that zombies will keep dragging the market down.
examples.cn: 经济学家警告说，这些僵而不死的企业会继续拖累市场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「走毙」——走着走着就倒毙了，却还立着；或是「糟毙」——状态糟糕得像僵尸；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 海地克里奥尔语 zombie（被巫术驱使的死尸）→ 英语 zombie；更早多归入班图语族，如 nzambi（神、灵），一般认为是来源之一，但未确证。核心义「身体还在动、生命已不在的影子」。

sensesIntro.en: Zombie starts as the revived dead of Caribbean belief, then becomes the tired lifeless person, the system that will not stop, the dead word, and the institution kept alive.
sensesIntro.cn: zombie 起初指加勒比信仰中复活的死者，再变成疲惫麻木的人、停不下来的系统、死去的旧词，以及靠外力续命的机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale figure shuffling forward with no life in its eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个脸色苍白、眼里没有生命、拖步前行的人形。

branches.en: The folklore corpse that walks is the source sense.
branches.cn: 传说中会走路的尸体是本义。

branches.en: An exhausted person acts like the walking dead.
branches.cn: 筋疲力尽的人举止如同活死人。

branches.en: A program that will not stop is a mechanical echo.
branches.cn: 停不下来的程序是这种形象的机械回声。

branches.en: A company kept alive by aid copies the revived body.
branches.cn: 靠补助续命的公司仿如被复活的躯体。

branches.en: A remembered but unused word is a corpse that still moves.
branches.cn: 被记住却不再使用的词，就是一具仍在走动的尸体。

intro.en: Zombie is a borrowed Caribbean noun; English builds zombify, zombification, and the early spelling zomby on it.
intro.cn: zombie 是从加勒比借来的名词，英语围绕它构成 zombify、zombification 以及早期拼法 zomby。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor: the word comes from Caribbean speech, with African language forms often suggested.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先：它来自加勒比地区的语言，常被认为与非洲语言形式有关。

items.example: The Haitian form zombi enters early reports.
items.exampleCN: 海地语的 zombi 最早出现在相关记述里。

items.example: Zombie is the standard English spelling.
items.exampleCN: zombie 是标准英语拼法。

items.example: The suffix -s forms zombies.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 构成 zombies。

items.example: Zombies fill the second half of the film.
items.exampleCN: zombies 出现在电影后半段。

items.example: The suffix -ify forms zombify.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ify 构成 zombify。

items.example: Long meetings zombify the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 冗长的会议让整个团队变得麻木。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms zombification.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 zombification。

items.example: Critics speak of the zombification of the news.
items.exampleCN: 评论者说新闻正在变得死气沉沉。

items.example: The early spelling zomby uses the suffix -y.
items.exampleCN: 早期拼法 zomby 用了后缀 -y。

items.example: Zomby appears in older travel writing.
items.exampleCN: zomby 出现在较早的游记中。

definition_zh: 动物学的；与动物学有关的；动物的
definition_en: relating to zoology, the scientific study of animals
core_image: 玻璃柜里钉着标签的甲虫标本，旁边是一页画满动物图谱的笔记
scene: 自然史博物馆的新展厅里，一排排玻璃柜陈列着鸟类骨骼与兽皮标本，每个柜子都挂着写满说明的标签。In the new hall of the natural history museum, visitors walk past rows of glass cases in a zoological collection, each label filled with careful notes.
sceneCN: 这里 zoological 是「动物学的、与动物学有关的」（第 1 个义项：关于动物学的）；句意：自然史博物馆新展厅里，参观者走过一个个「动物学收藏」的玻璃柜，每张标签都写满细致的记录。

pos.zh: 动物学的；与动物学有关的

collocations.zh: 动物园（zoo 的正式说法）
动物园园区；野生动物园

derivatives.zh: 在 zoo-（动物）后加 -logy（学科），义为「动物学」
在 zoology 后加 -ist（从事者），义为「动物学家」
zoological garden 的截短形式，义为「动物园」
加 -ly 构成副词，义为「从动物学角度」

senses.title: Relating to the science of animals
senses.definition: connected with zoology, the branch of biology that studies animals
senses.definitionCN: 与动物学（研究动物的生物学分科）相联系的
senses.example: She began her zoological research with a survey of local beetles.
senses.exampleCN: 她以当地甲虫的调查开始了自己的动物学研究。
senses.why: The first half of the word names animals and the second half names a field of study, so the ending -ical turns the whole into an adjective of that science.
senses.whyCN: 词的前半表示「动物」，后半表示「学问」，而词尾 -ical 把整个词变成「该门学问的」形容词，所以它天然指动物学。

senses.title: Of or about animals themselves
senses.definition: of or concerning animals, their species, or their features
senses.definitionCN: 关于动物本身、其种类或特征的
senses.example: The garden is famous for its rare zoological species.
senses.exampleCN: 这座园林以稀有的动物物种闻名。
senses.why: Because the animal part of the word is the core, the adjective can widen from the science to the animals it studies.
senses.whyCN: 词的核心是「动物」这一部分，所以形容词可以从「学科」放宽到学科所研究的「动物」本身。

senses.title: Used of institutions and collections
senses.definition: used in the names of museums, gardens, and societies devoted to animals
senses.definitionCN: 用于冠名博物馆、园林与学会等以动物为对象的机构
senses.example: The old zoological garden opened to the public in that decade.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老动物园在那个年代向公众开放了。
senses.why: Institutional names fixed the adjective in place, and the garden sense grew into the everyday word zoo.
senses.whyCN: 机构名称把这个形容词固定了下来，而「园林」这一用法又缩略成日常的 zoo，因此该词带着机构色彩。

senses.title: Describing classification and study methods
senses.titleCN: 动物分类与研究方法上的
senses.definition: describing the classifying, naming, or studying of animals in a scientific way
senses.definitionCN: 以科学方式对动物进行分类、命名或研究的
senses.example: Zoological taxonomy groups animals by shared features.
senses.exampleCN: 动物分类学按共同特征把动物分组。
senses.why: Science needs a precise adjective for its methods, so the word also labels classification, naming, and specimen practice.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要为方法找精确的形容词，于是这个词也用来修饰分类、命名与标本实践。

senses.title: Set in a formal or learned register
senses.definition: used instead of simpler words such as animal when a formal or academic tone is wanted
senses.definitionCN: 在需要正式或学术语气时替代 animal 这类更简单的词
senses.example: The committee prefers zoological terms in its formal reports.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在正式报告中更偏爱动物学用语。
senses.why: Institutions and journals favour the longer Latin-shaped adjective, giving it a learned tone over the plain word animal.
senses.whyCN: 机构与期刊偏爱这个更长的拉丁式形容词，使它比朴素的 animal 带有学术气。

senses.title: As part of a personal or place name
senses.titleCN: 姓名与机构名中的固定成分
senses.definition: appearing as a fixed word in society names, park names, and titles
senses.definitionCN: 作为学会名、公园名与称号中的固定成分出现
senses.example: The zoological society holds an open day each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家动物学会每年春天举办开放日。
senses.why: Once a name is registered it stops changing, so the adjective survives inside fixed titles even when the science moves on.
senses.whyCN: 名称一旦登记就很少改动，所以即便学科在演进，这个形容词仍以固定称号的形式存活下来。

intro.en: Zoological is the adjective of zoology, formed from Greek zoon, an animal, and logos, word or study, with the English adjective ending -ical added later.
intro.cn: zoological 是 zoology 的形容词，由希腊语 zoon（动物）与 logos（言语、学问）构成，后再加英语形容词词尾 -ical。

items.en: Zoon means a living creature; the related verb zoi means to live.
items.cn: zoōn 意为「活物、动物」；相关动词 zōein 意为「活着」。

items.en: Logos means word, account, or reasoned study.
items.cn: logos 意为「言语、论说、有道理的学问」。

items.en: Scholars first combined the two Greek roots into a Latin-shaped name for the study of animals.
items.cn: 学者们先把两个希腊词根拼成拉丁式名称，用来指动物研究。

items.en: The French form carries the term into the language of natural history.
items.cn: 法语形式把这一术语带进博物学的语言。

items.en: English first uses zoology and then adds -ical to form the adjective zoological.
items.cn: 英语先用 zoology，后加 -ical 构成形容词 zoological。

items.en: The clipped form zoo shortens the old phrase zoological garden in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪，截短形式 zoo 取代了旧说法 zoological garden。

note.en: Zoological belongs to the zoo- word family with zoology, zoologist, and zoo, and stands near the plain adjective animal.
note.cn: zoological 属于以 zoo- 为首的词族，同族有 zoology、zoologist 与 zoo，并在意义上靠近朴素的形容词 animal。

entries.definition: the scientific study of animals
entries.definitionCN: 动物学；zoological 正是由它派生而来

entries.definition: a specialist in the study of animals
entries.definitionCN: 动物学家；词族中以 -ist 表示从业者

entries.definition: a place where wild animals are kept and shown
entries.definitionCN: 动物园；截自旧短语 zoological garden，属同词族的口语短形式

entries.definition: relating to living creatures other than humans
entries.definitionCN: 动物的；比 zoological 更口语、更宽泛

entries.definition: relating to the study of living things
entries.definitionCN: 生物学的；范围更大，涵盖动植物

entries.definition: relating to the study of plants
entries.definitionCN: 植物学的；与动物学形成对照的姊妹学科

normalIntro.en: Zoological is built like a small formula: animal plus study plus adjective ending.
normalIntro.cn: zoological 像一个小公式：动物 + 学问 + 形容词词尾。

normal.en: Zoo- means animal: the same piece sits inside zoology and zoologist.
normal.cn: zoo- 表示动物：同一部分也出现在 zoology 与 zoologist 里。

normal.en: The ending -logy marks a field of study, as in biology and geology.
normal.cn: 词尾 -logy 标记一门学问，如 biology 与 geology。

normal.en: The suffix -ical changes a noun of study into an adjective.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ical 把表示学问的名词变成形容词。

normal.en: Zoological garden is the long formal name hiding inside the short word zoo.
normal.cn: 「zoological garden」是藏在短词 zoo 背后的正式全称。

normal.en: Pair it with botanical: animals against plants, ends of the same scientific mirror.
normal.cn: 与 botanical 配对记忆：动物对植物，是同一面科学镜子的两端。

abstract.en: See a pinned beetle under glass with a neat label in small print.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钉在玻璃下的小甲虫，标签上印着工整的小字。

abstract.en: Picture a long row of cages with name plates above each door.
abstract.cn: 想象一长排笼舍，每扇门上方都挂着名字牌。

abstract.en: Think of a heavy brass sign saying zoological garden on an iron gate.
abstract.cn: 想象铁门上挂着一块厚重的铜牌，写着动物园林的名号。

examples.en: The zoological garden was founded more than a century ago.
examples.cn: 这座动物园始建于一个多世纪以前。

examples.en: Her zoological interests began with insects in the local woods.
examples.cn: 她的动物学兴趣始于本地树林里的昆虫。

examples.en: Students visited the museum to study zoological specimens.
examples.cn: 学生们参观博物馆去研究动物标本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「租 + 逻辑 + 扣」——租个笼子、按逻辑装动物、再扣上盖子，就是讲动物学的地方；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 zoōn（活物、动物）+ logos（言语、学问），经拉丁式与法语形式进入英语，词尾 -ical 构成形容词，核心义「关于动物之学问的」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts with the science of animals, widens to animals in general, then settles into institutional names and methodological talk before taking on a formal tone.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词先指动物学这门学科，再放宽到动物本身，然后凝固在机构名称与方法术语里，最后带上正式、学术的语气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a labelled beetle under glass with a page of animal notes beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃下贴着标签的甲虫，旁边是一页动物笔记。

branches.en: The science sense is the first and most literal one.
branches.cn: 学科义是最直接、最本义的义项。

branches.en: The animal sense widens from the science to what it studies.
branches.cn: 动物义由学科放宽到学科研究的对象。

branches.en: Institutions fixed the word in names of gardens and societies.
branches.cn: 机构把这个词固定在园林与学会的名称里。

branches.en: Methodological and formal uses grow out of its academic shape.
branches.cn: 方法义与正式语气都源自它学术化的词形。

branches.en: The institutional branch survives as fixed titles in names.
branches.cn: 机构义以固定称号的形式在专名中存续。

intro.en: Zoological is built from the combining form zoo-, the suffix -logy, and the English adjective ending -ical.
intro.cn: zoological 由组合形式 zoo-、词尾 -logy 以及英语形容词词尾 -ical 搭成。

latinIntro.en: The roots are Greek rather than Latin, but later scientific Latin shaped the term before it reached English.
latinIntro.cn: 构词词根来自希腊语而非拉丁语，但近代科学拉丁语在它进入英语前塑造了这一术语。

items.example: Zoo- opens words such as zoology and zooplankton.
items.exampleCN: zoo- 构成 zoology、zooplankton 等词的开头。

items.example: The suffix -logy marks a field of learning.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -logy 标记一门学问。

items.example: The ending -ical turns zoology into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ical 把 zoology 变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms zoologist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 zoologist。

items.example: The ending -ly forms zoologically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 zoologically。

items.example: Zoology is the base noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: zoology 是这个词族的基础名词。

items.example: A zoologist studies animals in the field or the lab.
items.exampleCN: 动物学家在野外或实验室里研究动物。

items.meaning: a place where animals are shown
items.example: Zoo is a clipped form of the long phrase.
items.exampleCN: zoo 是长短语的截短形式。

items.meaning: relating to the study of animals
items.example: Zoological keeps the full academic shape.
items.exampleCN: zoological 保留了完整的学术词形。

items.meaning: from a zoological point of view
items.example: Zoologically speaking, the two species are close.
items.exampleCN: 从动物学角度看，这两个物种很接近。

latinEntries.example: Animal is the Latin word behind English animal.
latinEntries.exampleCN: animal 是英语 animal 的拉丁语来源词。

latinEntries.example: Zoon entered scientific Latin and then technical English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: zoōn 先进入科学拉丁语，再进入技术英语。

definition_zh: 动物学；动物学的著作或论述；动物的总体特征
definition_en: the scientific study of animals, including their structure, behaviour, and classification
core_image: 一张实验台上摊开的动物图册，旁边放着解剖镜与装着标本的小玻璃瓶
scene: 大学里的动物学系课程表中，上午是解剖实验课，下午是野外观察；任课教师强调，先学会辨识物种，才能谈行为与分类。In the timetable of the department of zoology, mornings are given to dissection classes and afternoons to field observation, and the teacher insists that species must be recognised before behaviour can be discussed.
sceneCN: 这里 zoology 是「动物学」（第 1 个义项：研究动物的科学门类）；句意：在动物学系的课程表中，上午安排解剖课，下午进行野外观察，教师坚持要先能辨识物种，才谈得上讨论行为。

动物学著作；动物学论述
动物的总体；动物的特征

senses.title: The science that studies animals
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies the form, behaviour, and classification of animals
senses.definitionCN: 研究动物的形态、行为与分类的生物学分科
senses.example: She studied zoology before turning to conservation.
senses.exampleCN: 她先学习动物学，后来转向自然保护工作。
senses.why: The Greek animal root joined to the study suffix produces a name for a whole discipline, not for one animal.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语的「动物」词根与表示「学问」的后缀结合，产出的是一门完整学科的名称，而不是某一种动物。

senses.title: Written work on animals
senses.titleCN: 动物学著作；动物学论述
senses.definition: a book or body of writing that treats animals in a scientific way
senses.definitionCN: 以科学方式论述动物的著作或全部文字成果
senses.example: His zoology contains a full chapter on insect wings.
senses.exampleCN: 他的动物学著作里有一整章讲昆虫的翅膀。
senses.why: Field names of study often also stand for the books written in that field, so the noun can mean a treatise rather than a subject.
senses.whyCN: 学科名称常常也指该领域的著作，因此这个名词可以指一部论著而不只是指学科本身。

senses.title: The animals of a place
senses.titleCN: 某地的动物总体；动物区系
senses.definition: the collective animals of a particular region or period
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区或某一时期动物的总体
senses.example: The zoology of the island is rich in small mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛屿的动物区系中多小哺乳动物。
senses.why: From the science the noun shifts to its object, naming the whole animal population that the science examines.
senses.whyCN: 词义从学科转向研究对象，指该学科所考察的整个动物群体。

senses.title: A course or subject at school
senses.definition: the subject as it is taught, examined, or listed in a timetable
senses.definitionCN: 作为课程、考试科目或课表条目出现的动物学
senses.example: Zoology is a required subject for biology students.
senses.exampleCN: 动物学是生物专业学生的必修科目。
senses.why: A discipline becomes a classroom subject, so the same noun names a course, a syllabus, and an exam paper.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科进入课堂就变成课程，于是同一个名词也指科目、课程纲要与试卷。

senses.title: The department or academic field
senses.definition: the institution or professional field gathered under this name
senses.definitionCN: 以此命名的机构或专业领域
senses.example: The zoology department has just appointed two new lecturers.
senses.exampleCN: 动物学系刚刚聘任了两位新讲师。
senses.why: Institutional usage turns the science into a place, a department, or a professional circle where the work is carried out.
senses.whyCN: 机构性的用法把学科变成一个场所、院系或专业圈子，工作在那里展开。

senses.title: A division within biology
senses.definition: one of the main branches of biology, shown against others such as botany
senses.definitionCN: 作为生物学主要分科之一，与植物学等并列
senses.example: Modern zoology borrows methods from genetics and ecology.
senses.exampleCN: 现代动物学从遗传学与生态学中借用方法。
senses.why: Once placed in a wider system of sciences, the noun marks a branch that is defined by what it excludes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被放进更大的科学体系，这个名词就标出一个由「研究什么、不研究什么」来界定的分科。

senses.title: Animals as a subject of general description
senses.definition: the general knowledge or description of animal life as a subject of curiosity
senses.definitionCN: 作为好奇心对象的动物生活知识或描述
senses.example: The children were drawn to zoology through picture books.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们是通过图画书对动物知识产生兴趣的。
senses.why: The plain interest in animals survives under the academic name, so the word can carry a lighter sense of knowing about animal life.
senses.whyCN: 对动物的朴素兴趣仍藏在学术名称之下，于是这个词也能带上「了解动物生活」的轻松含义。

intro.en: Zoology joins Greek zoon, an animal, to the study suffix -logia, a combination first made in modern Latin and then passed through French into English in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: zoology 把希腊语 zoōn（动物）与表示学问的后缀 -logia 结合，这一组合先在近代拉丁语中形成，再经法语在十七世纪进入英语。

items.en: Zoon means a living creature or animal.
items.cn: zoōn 意为「活物、动物」。

items.en: Logia means a collection of reasoned words or the study of something.
items.cn: logia 意为「成套的论说」或「对某物的研究」。

items.en: Early scientists build Latin-shaped names for the growing sciences.
items.cn: 早期科学家为不断分化的学科造出拉丁式名称。

items.en: A French form of the term appears among early naturalists.
items.cn: 该术语的法语形式在早期博物学者中出现。

items.en: English takes the word and applies it to the study of animals.
items.cn: 英语借用该词，用它指对动物的研究。

items.en: The word settles into university departments and scientific writing.
items.cn: 这个词最终固定为大学院系与科学写作中的用语。

note.en: Zoology shares the zoon root with zoologist and zoological, and stands in the biology family beside botany and ecology.
note.cn: zoology 与 zoologist、zoological 共享 zoon 这一词根，并与 botany、ecology 同处生物学一族。

entries.definition: a person who studies animals as a science
entries.definitionCN: 动物学家；同一词根上加 -ist 指从业者

entries.definition: relating to the study of animals
entries.definitionCN: 动物学的；与 zoology 同根，只是词尾不同

entries.definition: a ring of constellations used for astrology
entries.definitionCN: 黄道带；与动物学无关，只是拼写以 zo 开头、词源不同

entries.definition: the broad study of living things
entries.definitionCN: 生物学；范围更大，包含动物学

entries.definition: the scientific study of plants
entries.definitionCN: 植物学；与动物学并列的姊妹学科

entries.definition: the study of how living things relate to their surroundings
entries.definitionCN: 生态学；关注动物与环境的关系

normalIntro.en: Zoology is a two-part name: the animal root plus the study suffix, the same pattern as biology and geology.
normalIntro.cn: zoology 是两段式名称：动物词根加学问后缀，和 biology、geology 的构词方式一样。

normal.en: Zoo- marks the animal part, as in zoologist and zoological.
normal.cn: zoo- 标出「动物」这一部分，如 zoologist 与 zoological。

normal.en: The suffix -logy marks a field of study, shared with biology and psychology.
normal.cn: 词尾 -logy 标记学问，与 biology、psychology 共用。

normal.en: Zoology is the science; zoologist is the person; zoological is the adjective.
normal.cn: zoology 是学科，zoologist 是从业者，zoological 是形容词。

normal.en: The short word zoo is clipped from zoological garden, a sibling of the family.
normal.cn: 短词 zoo 截自「zoological garden」，属于同一词族。

normal.en: Pair zoology with botany: one studies animals, the other plants.
normal.cn: 把 zoology 与 botany 配对：一个研究动物，一个研究植物。

abstract.en: See a notebook open at a drawing of a beetle and a microscope beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本翻到甲虫绘图处的笔记本，旁边放着显微镜。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of thick volumes, each spine saying zoology.
abstract.cn: 想象一整排厚重的书，每本书脊上都印着动物学。

abstract.en: Think of a map dotted with tiny animal icons, one for every region.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，上面点点小动物图标，每个地区一个。

examples.en: He chose zoology because he wanted to understand animal behaviour.
examples.cn: 他选择动物学，是因为想弄懂动物的行为。

examples.en: Modern zoology relies on genetics as much as on field notes.
examples.cn: 现代动物学对遗传学的依赖不亚于对野外笔记的依赖。

examples.en: The island zoology includes several species found nowhere else.
examples.cn: 该岛的动物区系包含几个别处找不到的物种。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「租 + 逻辑」——租个场地、按逻辑把动物分门别类，就是动物学；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 zoōn（活物、动物）+ -logia（论说、学问）→ 近代拉丁语与法语形式 → 英语 zoology，核心义「关于动物的学问」。

sensesIntro.en: Zoology names a science, then the books written in that science, then the animals it covers, and finally the courses, departments, and branches it fills.
sensesIntro.cn: zoology 先指一门科学，再指这门科学写成的著作，随后指它所涵盖的动物，最后指由它填满的课程、院系与分科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open animal atlas beside a dissection scope and jars of specimens.
core.cn: 核心意象：摊开的动物图册旁放着解剖镜与标本瓶。

branches.en: The science sense is the literal core of the word.
branches.cn: 学科义是这个词最本义的核。

branches.en: From the science comes the name for its books.
branches.cn: 由学科引申出对学科著作的称谓。

branches.en: The object of study becomes a sense of its own.
branches.cn: 研究对象本身也成了一个义项。

branches.en: Teaching and institutions turn the science into courses and departments.
branches.cn: 教学与机构把学科变成课程与院系。

branches.en: The branch sense and the general-knowledge sense both circle the same animal root.
branches.cn: 分科义与一般知识义都围绕同一个「动物」词根。

intro.en: Zoology is built from the combining form zoo- and the study suffix -logy, with zoologist, zoological, and zoo around it.
intro.cn: zoology 由组合形式 zoo- 与表示学问的词尾 -logy 构成，周围有 zoologist、zoological 与 zoo。

latinIntro.en: The roots are Greek, but the term was assembled in scientific Latin before French and English took it up.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自希腊语，但这个术语是在科学拉丁语中拼合而成，之后才被法语与英语采用。

items.example: Zoo- heads words such as zoology and zoogeography.
items.exampleCN: zoo- 位于 zoology、zoogeography 等词的首部。

items.example: The suffix -logy names an academic field.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -logy 为学术领域命名。

items.meaning: a collection of words or a study
items.example: The Greek ending -logia is the earlier form of -logy.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语词尾 -logia 是 -logy 的更早形式。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms zoologist from zoology.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 把 zoology 变成 zoologist。

items.example: The ending -ical forms zoological.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ical 构成 zoological。

items.example: The suffix -graphy combines with zoo- in zoogeography.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -graphy 与 zoo- 组合成 zoogeography。

items.example: Zoology keeps the full Greek shape in English.
items.exampleCN: zoology 在英语中保留了完整的希腊词形。

items.example: A zoologist may work in a museum or in the field.
items.exampleCN: 动物学家可能在博物馆或野外工作。

items.example: Zoological is the adjective partner of zoology.
items.exampleCN: zoological 是 zoology 的形容词伙伴。

items.meaning: a place where animals are shown
items.example: Zoo is the short cousin of the family.
items.exampleCN: zoo 是这个词族里的小表亲。

latinEntries.example: Zoon provides the animal first half of the term.
latinEntries.exampleCN: zoōn 提供了术语中表示「动物」的前半部分。

latinEntries.example: Zoologia is the Latin shape of the term.
latinEntries.exampleCN: zoologia 是该术语的拉丁语形式。
